text:
jonah: hey team, first day here. using Windows 11 (native, not WSL) and trying to follow the onboarding. i installed scoop and chocolatey because some tools prefer one over the other. problems: asdf seems to be installed under WSL in the docs but i want asdf on native Windows for ruby/python/node. also Pageant/putty vs OpenSSH key issues for git/ssh, and op signin for 1password kept failing in powershell. any quick tips?

maya: welcome! on Windows we usually recommend using WSL2 for asdf to avoid path/link issues. but if you need native, use the asdf-win fork or rely on asdf bash via Git Bash/msys2. for native PowerShell, the simplest is to use "asdf via WSL" and mount your repo into WSL, or use `scoop install asdf-vm` if you must.

trent: for SSH, Windows has two worlds: OpenSSH (built-in) and PuTTY/Pageant. If your org uses Pageant, set your git to use plink: `git config --global core.sshCommand "plink -agent -i C:/Users/You/.ssh/id_ed25519.ppk"`. Otherwise convert key to OpenSSH format and enable the OpenSSH agent service: `Set-Service ssh-agent -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service ssh-agent; ssh-add C:\Users\You\.ssh\id_ed25519` in an elevated PowerShell.

jonah: i converted the key with puttygen to .ppk and tried plink but git still prompts for password. i see `Permission denied (publickey)` when pushing.

maya: double-check Pageant is running and loaded with the .ppk. use `pageant -list` to see identities. For plink, ensure `GIT_SSH` or `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` is pointing to plink.exe. Also check your ~/.ssh/config doesn't override to use a different key.

jonah: 1password `op signin` in PowerShell complains about missing `bash` for some helpers in our bootstrap script. is there a supported flow for PowerShell?

trent: run `op signin --raw` in PowerShell and capture token: `$token = op signin --account my --raw` then `setx OP_SESSION_my $token` for that user session, or `powershell -NoProfile -Command "$env:OP_SESSION_my='$(op signin --raw)'; ..."` in scripts. Avoid storing tokens long-term.

maya: if you use devcontainer on Windows host, prefer launching container from WSL. Containers launched from Windows can have permission/path issues and won't pick up WSL-installed asdf. For GUI terminals like Windows Terminal, set default profile to WSL for dev work.

jonah: got it. one more thing: my PowerShell profile wasn't loading environment vars set by the dotfiles script. any recommendation for hooking dotfiles into Windows shells?

trent: add bootstrap lines to both `%USERPROFILE%\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1` and `~/.git-bashrc` depending on which shell you use. For Scoop-installed tools, ensure `C:\Users\You\scoop\shims` is early in PATH.

infra-bot: If you need corporate certs or VPN config for git to reach internal remotes, open REQ-2099 and infra will provision. Also note we prefer WSL2 for reproducible builds.

jonah: thanks all! i'll try WSL asdf for now, convert my key to OpenSSH and enable ssh-agent, and use op signin --raw in PowerShell. will report back if anything else pops up. really appreciate the quick help :pray:
